'''John Adrian Bondy''' (born 1944) is a retired English mathematician, known for his work in [[combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]].

==Career==

Bondy received his Ph.D. in [[graph theory]] from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1969. His advisor was [[Dominic Welsh]].<ref name="genealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=23492}}</ref> Between 1969 and 1994, Bondy was ''Professor of Graph Theory'' at the [[University of Waterloo]] in Canada, and then, until his retirement, at [[Université Lyon 1]] in France.<ref name="birthday">{{cite web|last1=Charbit|first1=Pierre|last2=Havet|first2=Frédéric|title=A conference in Honor of Adrian Bondy for his 70th Birthday|url=https://www.irif.fr/~charbit/Bondyis70/bondy70.html|access-date=18 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117003424/https://www.irif.fr/~charbit/Bondyis70/bondy70.html|archive-date=17 January 2022|date=2014}}</ref> From 1976, he was managing editor, and, between 1979 and 2004, co-editor-in-chief (together with [[U. S. R. Murty]]) of [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B]].<ref>{{Harvtxt|Cunningham|Haxell|Richter|Wormald|2004}}</ref> Throughout his career, Bondy has (co-)authored over 100 publications<ref name="birthday"/><ref>{{cite web|title=MR: Bondy, John Adrian - 39150|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=39150|url-access=subscription|access-date=19 September 2022}}</ref> with 51 co-authors,<ref>{{cite web|title=MR: Co-authors of Bondy, John Adrian|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/authors.html?coauth=39150|url-access=subscription|access-date=19 September 2022}}</ref> including the widely influential textbook ''Graph Theory with Applications'' (with [[U. S. R. Murty]]), and supervised 12 Ph.D. students.<ref name="genealogy" /> His [[Erdős number]] is 1.<ref>{{Harvtxt|Bondy|Erdős|1973}}</ref>

Bondy was dismissed from his tenured position at the University of Waterloo in 1995, after 25 years in which he had been a major contributor to the renown of the University's Department of Combinatorics and Optimization.<ref>{{cite web |title=UW Gazette - Arbitrator upholds math prof's dismissal |date=October 2, 1996 |url=http://www.communications.uwaterloo.ca/Gazette/1996/October02/Arbitrator%20upholds%20math%20prof%27s%20dismissal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427141236/http://www.communications.uwaterloo.ca/Gazette/1996/October02/Arbitrator%20upholds%20math%20prof%27s%20dismissal |archive-date=April 27, 2012}}</ref> The reasons for his dismissal centered on ''"Bondy's acceptance of a teaching post in France, and the acceptability of someone who is on UW's faculty payroll holding a full-time job elsewhere."''<ref>{{cite web |title=UW Gazette - Faculty dismissal discussed |date=September 20, 1995 |url=http://www.communications.uwaterloo.ca/Gazette/1995/Gazette%2C%20September%2020%2C%201995/Faculty%20dismissal%20case%20discussed/Front%20page:%20professor%20is%20identified |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101123220541/http://www.communications.uwaterloo.ca/Gazette/1995/Gazette,%20September%2020,%201995/Faculty%20dismissal%20case%20discussed/Front%20page:%20professor%20is%20identified |archive-date=November 23, 2010}}</ref> Protesting the decision, [[Paul Erdős]] returned his honorary doctorate to the University of Waterloo,<ref>{{cite web|last1=Erdős|first1=Paul|author-link1=Paul Erdős|title=Dear President Downey|url=http://ecp6.jussieu.fr/pageperso/bondy/uw/letters/erdos.pdf|access-date=8 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051015141515/http://ecp6.jussieu.fr/pageperso/bondy/uw/letters/erdos.pdf|archive-date=15 October 2005|date=4 June 1996|quote=With a heavy heart I feel that I have to sever my connections with the University of Waterloo, including resigning my honorary degree which I received from the University in 1981 (which caused me great pleasure). I was very upset by the treatment of Professor Adrian Bondy. I do not maintain that Professor Bondy was innocent, but in view of his accomplishments and distinguished services to the University I feel that 'justice should be tempered with mercy.'}}</ref> and [[Vašek Chvátal]] resigned from his position of ''Adjunct Professor'' at the Department of Combinatorics and Optimization.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Chvátal|first1=Václav|author-link1=Vašek Chvátal|title=An Open Letter Submitted to the Gazette|url=https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/6621/gazette.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210808191250/https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/6621/gazette.pdf|archive-date=2021-08-08|date=20 September 1995|access-date=2022-09-19}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Bondy has a passion for [[photography]], having taken pictures since his childhood. In the 1980s, he regularly exhibited his work, most notably at the ''Kitchener-Waterloo Art Gallery'' in [[Kitchener, Ontario]]. In 2010, Bondy founded the non-profit association ''Mind's Eye''<ref>{{cite web|title=Mind's Eye|url=https://en.mindseye.fr/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918214012/https://en.mindseye.fr/|archive-date=18 September 2022|access-date=19 September 2022}}</ref> with the aim ''"to reflect upon the conceptual links between mathematics and photography."''<ref>{{cite web|title=Mind's Eye - Adrian Bondy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210519014206/https://en.mindseye.fr/Bondy.php|archive-date=19 May 2021|url=https://en.mindseye.fr/Bondy.php|access-date=19 September 2022}}</ref> In 2012, he opened a photo gallery with the same name on the [[Rue Saint-Jacques, Paris]]. Between 2012 and 2022, ''Mind's Eye / Galerie Adrian Bondy'' has hosted 42 exhibitions with works of 27 artists, including [[John Claridge]] and [[Jean Dréville]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mind's Eye - Exhibitions|url=https://en.mindseye.fr/EXHIBITIONS.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918213932/https://en.mindseye.fr/EXHIBITIONS.php|archive-date=18 September 2022|access-date=19 September 2022}}</ref>
